title: 16S rRNA sequencing raw data from a thermophilic trickle bed reactor for biogas upgrading
author: Getachew Birhanu Abera

materials: The filtered inoculum then underwent two-week of degassing procedure in a shaking incubator at 90 rpm to remove residual organic matter at both mesophilic (37 ºC) and thermophilic (51 °C) temperatures. The degassed inoculum was then mixed with 10% (v/v) nutrient solution. This solution contained 408×10 −3 g/L KH 2 PO 4 , 426×10 −3 g/L Na 2 HPO 4 , 110×10 −3 g/L CaCl 2 ×2H 2 O, 100×10 −3 g/L MgCl 2 ×6H 2 O, 300×10 −3 g/L NH 4 Cl, 300×10 −3 g/L NaCl and 1 mL/L of trace elements. The trace elements were prepared by mixing 1500 mg/L FeCl 2 . 4H 2 O, 70 mg/L ZnCl 2 , 100 mg/L MnCl 2 × 4H 2 O, 6 mg/L H 3 BO 3 , 190 mg/L CoCl 2 × 6H 2 O, 2 mg/L CuCl 2 × 2H 2 O, 24 mg/L NiCl 2 ×6H 2 O and 36 mg/L Na 2 MoO 4 × 2H 2 O. Two laboratory-scale TBRs with a working volume of 815 mL were utilized to further investigate the impact of H 2 S on biomethanation. One of the TBR is assigned as control (TBR-Control) and the other as test (TBR-H 2 S). The TBRs were filled with 145g of polyethylene biocarriers CFAS ® (surface area=650 m 2 /m 3 ) (Biowater Technology AS, Norway). The TBRs were inoculated with 150 mL of degassed inoculum (containing 10% v/v nutrients solution) and supplied with biogas with a mixture of CH 4 , CO 2 , and H 2 . The gas injection was done at the bottom of the reactor in a counter-current direction through a fish stone diffuser with a gas loading of 3.68 L/L reactor . d in 4:1 H 2 to CO 2 ratio, respectively . The substrate gas flow was controlled by a mass flow controller (MC 50, Alicat Scientific, Tucson, AZ 85743, U.S.A.). The recirculation of inoculum was carried out continuously at a rate of 60 mL/min using a peristaltic pump (530 DU, Watson-Marlow Limited, UK). The reactors were maintained at a thermophilic temperature of 51 ºC by recirculating water through the reactor water jacket from a water bath (CORIO CD-BC4 heating circulator, JULABO GmbH, Germany). The temperature of the room was continuously monitored using a digital thermometer attached to near the TBRs ((EL-WiFi-TP Wireless Temperature Data Loggers, Ohio, U.SA.). The experiment lasted 220 days and every week 30 mL of liquid was removed and replaced with the same volume of new degassed inoculum to provide a continuous source of nutrients for the microbes and prevent buildup of inhibitory compounds. Excess water generated during the process was also removed to maintain the same level of liquids throughout the experiment. The experiment was conducted in two consecutive periods (Period-I and II). The purpose of Period-I was to acclimatize the methanogens inside the inoculum with a mixture of the substrate gases (containing H 2 , CH 4 and CO 2 ) and promote them to produce stable CH 4 content in both reactors before the commencement of H 2 S experiment. The Period-II was specifically designed to assess the effect of H 2 S on biomethanation and microbial community structure. The TBR experiment was conducted in two periods as described below: Period I (adaptation period) : During this period, both TBRs were supplied and acclimatized with H 2 and biogas containing 60% CH 4 and 40% CO 2 (H 2 : CO 2 ratio = 4:1). The gas loading was 3.68 L/ L reactor .d and the gas retention time (GRT) was 6.52 hrs. The substrate gas composition injected after mixing during this period was 62% H 2 , 15% CO2 and 23% CH 4 . This period aimed to facilitate the formation of biofilm on the packing material and to acclimate to the input gas. The adaptation period (Period I) lasted 120 days. The average normalized CH 4 content (%) was considered stabilized when it remained constant for 8-10 consecutive days, signalling the beginning of the test period (Period II). The average CH 4 content and yield data for this period are included in this study. Period II (experimental period) : During this period, TBR-Control continued with the same gas composition and loading as in Period I. TBR-H 2 S was injected with H 2 and H 2 S-rich biogas containing 57% CH 4 , 40% CO 2 , and 3% H 2 S (H 2 : CO 2 ratio = 4:1), with a gas loading of 3.68 L/L reactor .d and GRT of 6.52 hrs. The gas composition injected into TBR-H 2 S in this period was 61.54% H 2 , 15.38% CO 2 , 21.92% CH 4 , and 1.15% H 2 S. The experimental period (Period II) lasted 100 days. During Period II, the gas volume from TBR-H 2 S could not be accurately measured due to safety concerns (high H 2 S content from the effluent gas, over 13,000ppm). Consequently, the performance of TBR-H 2 S was assessed based on the composition of the effluent gas. The effluent gas volume was assumed to be like that of TBR-Control, given that the input gas loading and composition were comparable. Samples for microbial analysis were stored in 2 mL Eppendorf tubes at -18ºC to preserve microbial integrity (Poulsen et al., 2021). One sample was taken from the adaptation period, and four samples (Day 4, 32, 46,

were taken during the experimental period (Day 4, 32, 46, 60). Microbial community analysis was conducted by DNASense (DNASense, Niels Jernes Vej 10, 9220 Aalborg, Denmark). The DNA extraction followed by method adapted from Jensen et al. (2023), utilizing the DNeasy 96 PowerSoil Pro QIAcube HT Kit. Each sample was mixed with 500 μL of CD1 solution and subjected to bead beating at 1600 rpm for two minutes, repeated three times with breaks of two minutes on ice in between. Following lysis, samples were centrifuged at 3500 x g for ten minutes. The supernatant of each sample was transferred to a new S-block well and mixed with CD2 and nuclease-free water in a 3:3:1 (v/v) ratio. After mixing, the samples were centrifuged again at 3500 x g for 10 minutes, and the process continued accordingly. Analysis and reporting were performed using DNASense’s custom bioinformatic workflow (version MCA_ONT_DS230723 ). Amplicon libraries for the 16S/18S rRNA gene variable regions 48 (abeV48A) were prepared using a custom protocol. Up to 25 ng of extracted DNA was used as a template for PCR amplification. Each PCR reaction (50 μL) contained 0.2 mM dNTP mix, 0.01 units of Platinum SuperFi DNA Polymerase (Thermo Fisher Scientific, U.S.A.), and 500 nM of each forward and reverse primer in the supplied SuperFI Buffer. PCR was done with the following program: Initial denaturation at 98 °C for 3 min, 25 cycles of amplification (98 ºC for 30 s, 62 ºC for 20 s, 72 ºC for 2 min), and a final elongation at 72 ºC for 5 min. The forward and reverse primers used include custom 24 nt barcode sequences followed by the sequences targeting abeV48A: [515FB] GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA and [1391R] GACGGGCGGTGWGTRCA (Apprill et al., 2015; Parada et al., 2016). The resulting amplicon libraries were purified using the standard protocol for CleanNGS SPRI beads (CleanNA, NL) with a bead-to-sample ratio of 3:

Subsequently, DNA was eluted in 25 μL of nuclease free water (Qiagen, Germany). Sequencing libraries were then prepared from the purified amplicon libraries using the SQKLSK114 kit (Oxford Nanopore Technologies, UK) following the manufacturer’s protocol with the following modifications: 500 ng total DNA was used as input, and CleanNGS SPRI beads were employed for library cleanup steps. DNA concentration was measured using the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, U.S.A.). A subset of amplicon libraries underwent validation for product size and purity through Gel electrophoresis using Tapestation 2200 and D1000/High sensitivity D1000 screentapes (Agilent, U.S.A.). The resulting sequencing library was loaded onto a MinION R10.4.1 flowcell and sequenced using the MinKNOW 23.04.6 software (Oxford Nanopore Technologies, UK). steps.title: Collect and filter inoculum
steps.instruction: Collect inoculum from 15 L manure‑based CSTRs operated at 51 °C, filter through a 0.212 mm sieve, then measure total solids (3.00 ± 0.01 %) and volatile solids (1.82 ± 0.01 %) by APHA (2017) and record pH (7).

steps.title: Degas inoculum
steps.instruction: Place filtered inoculum in a shaking incubator at 90 rpm for two weeks at both 37 °C (mesophilic) and 51 °C (thermophilic) to remove residual organic matter.

steps.title: Prepare nutrient solution
steps.instruction: Make a 10 % (v/v) nutrient solution containing per litre: 408 × 10⁻³ g KH₂PO₄, 426 × 10⁻³ g Na₂HPO₄, 110 × 10⁻³ g CaCl₂·2H₂O, 100 × 10⁻³ g MgCl₂·6H₂O, 300 × 10⁻³ g NH₄Cl, 300 × 10⁻³ g NaCl, and 1 mL trace‑element mix (1500 mg L⁻¹ FeCl₂·4H₂O, 70 mg L⁻¹ ZnCl₂, 100 mg L⁻¹ MnCl₂·4H₂O, 6 mg L⁻¹ H₃BO₃, 190 mg L⁻¹ CoCl₂·6H₂O, 2 mg L⁻¹ CuCl₂·2H₂O, 24 mg L⁻¹ NiCl₂·6H₂O, 36 mg L⁻¹ Na₂MoO₄·2H₂O).

steps.title: Mix inoculum with nutrients
steps.instruction: Combine the degassed inoculum with the nutrient solution at 10 % (v/v).

steps.title: Set up trickle‑bed reactors
steps.instruction: Fill two laboratory‑scale TBRs (815 mL working volume) with 145 g polyethylene biocarriers CFAS® (surface area = 650 m² m⁻³). Inoculate each reactor with 150 mL of the 10 % nutrient‑mixed degassed inoculum.

steps.title: Configure gas supply and recirculation
steps.instruction: Supply biogas (CH₄, CO₂, H₂) through a fish‑stone diffuser at the reactor bottom in counter‑current flow, using a gas loading of 3.68 L L⁻¹ reactor d⁻¹ with an H₂ : CO₂ ratio of 4 : 1. Control flow with an MC‑50 mass‑flow controller (Alicat). Recirculate inoculum continuously at 60 mL min⁻¹ with a peristaltic pump (530 DU, Watson‑Marlow). Maintain reactor temperature at 51 °C via a water jacket connected to a CORIO CD‑BC4 heating circulator (JULABO). Monitor room temperature with an EL‑WiFi‑TP wireless data logger.

steps.title: Run experiment and weekly maintenance
steps.instruction: Operate the reactors for 220 days. Each week remove 30 mL liquid and replace with the same volume of fresh degassed inoculum to supply nutrients and prevent inhibitor buildup; also remove excess water to keep liquid level constant.

steps.title: Period I – adaptation
steps.instruction: For the first 120 days both reactors receive gas with 60 % CH₄, 40 % CO₂, and H₂ such that the injected mixture after mixing is 62 % H₂, 15 % CO₂, 23 % CH₄ (overall H₂ : CO₂ = 4 : 1), gas loading 3.68 L L⁻¹ d⁻¹, and gas retention time 6.52 h. Continue until CH₄ content stabilises for 8–10 consecutive days.

steps.title: Period II – H₂S test
steps.instruction: For the next 100 days keep TBR‑Control on the same gas as Period I. Feed TBR‑H₂S with H₂ and H₂S‑rich biogas containing 57 % CH₄, 40 % CO₂, 3 % H₂S (overall H₂ : CO₂ = 4 : 1), gas loading 3.68 L L⁻¹ d⁻¹, GRT 6.52 h. The actual injected composition to TBR‑H₂S is 61.54 % H₂, 15.38 % CO₂, 21.92 % CH₄, 1.15 % H₂S. Assume effluent gas volume equals that of the control because direct measurement is unsafe (H₂S > 13 000 ppm).

steps.title: Collect microbial samples
steps.instruction: During the adaptation period take one sample; during Period II take samples on Days 4, 32, 46, 60. Store each 2 mL sample in an Eppendorf tube at –18 °C.

steps.title: Extract DNA
steps.instruction: Using the DNeasy 96 PowerSoil Pro QIAcube HT Kit, add 500 µL CD1 to each sample, bead‑beat at 1600 rpm for 2 min, repeat three times with 2‑min ice breaks. Centrifuge at 3500 × g for 10 min, transfer supernatant to a new S‑block well, add CD2 and nuclease‑free water in a 3 : 3 : 1 (v/v) ratio, mix, then centrifuge again at 3500 × g for 10 min. Continue the kit‑specified protocol thereafter.

steps.title: PCR amplification of 16S/18S V4‑V9
steps.instruction: Use up to 25 ng extracted DNA per 50 µL PCR: 0.2 mM dNTP mix, 0.01 U Platinum SuperFi DNA Polymerase (Thermo Fisher), 500 nM each forward (515FB GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA) and reverse (1391R GACGGGCGGTGWGTRCA) primer with custom 24‑nt barcodes, in supplied SuperFI buffer. Thermal program: 98 °C 3 min; 25 cycles of 98 °C 30 s, 62 °C 20 s, 72 °C 2 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min.

steps.title: Purify amplicon libraries
steps.instruction: Clean PCR products with CleanNGS SPRI beads at a bead‑to‑sample ratio of 3 : 1, then elute DNA in 25 µL nuclease‑free water (Qiagen).

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Using the SQK‑LSK114 kit (Oxford Nanopore), input 500 ng purified amplicon DNA, perform library cleanup with CleanNGS SPRI beads, and measure final DNA concentration with the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay kit (Thermo Fisher).

steps.title: Validate library size
steps.instruction: Run a subset of libraries on a Tapestation 2200 with D1000/High‑sensitivity D1000 screentapes (Agilent) to check product size and purity.

steps.title: Load and run MinION sequencing
steps.instruction: Load the library onto a MinION R10.4.1 flowcell, run with MinKNOW 23.04.6. Basecall and demultiplex using Guppy g6.5.7 with the super‑accurate config r10.4.1_400bps_sup.cfg and custom barcodes.

steps.title: Filter raw reads
steps.instruction: Filter demultiplexed fastq files with filtlong v0.2.1 using settings –min_length 320 –max_length 2000 –min_mean_q (value as specified in the original protocol). Retain reads 320–2000 bp with phred quality score > (as specified).

steps.title: Map reads to MiDAS database
steps.instruction: Map filtered reads to the QIIME‑formatted MiDAS release 4.8.1 using minimap2 v2.24‑r1122 with the –ax ‑mapont option, then process alignments with samtools v1.

steps.title: Clean taxonomy and filter mappings
steps.instruction: Edit the taxonomy flat file to replace entries containing ‘uncultured’, ‘metagenome’ or ‘unassigned’ with blanks. Filter mapping results to keep only alignments where query‑sequence length relative to alignment length deviates by 0.

steps.title: Identify low‑abundance OTUs
steps.instruction: Note low‑abundance OTUs as described in the original analysis (details omitted in the source text).
